title: Azure Cache for Redis from C#
description: Speed up ASP.NET Core responses by caching data in Azure Cache for Redis.

data.text: Azure Cache for Redis is a managed Redis cache. It is commonly used for session state, frequently queried reference data, rate limiting, and pub/sub messaging.

data.title: Create a Redis cache with Azure CLI
data.content: Choose Basic or Standard depending on SLA needs.
data.code:
az redis create \
  --name aspnet-redis-cache \
  --resource-group azure-for-aspnet-rg \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Basic \
  --vm-size c0

data.text: `StackExchange.Redis` is the standard C# Redis client. Use it directly or through the ASP.NET Core distributed cache abstraction.

data.title: Cache a database query result

data.text: Always plan how cached data becomes stale. Common invalidation strategies include time-to-live, event-driven invalidation, and cache-aside writes.

items: Set a reasonable absolute or sliding expiration
Remove or update cache entries when the underlying data changes
Do not cache sensitive user data without encryption or short TTLs

data.title: Cache the top posts endpoint
data.description: Reduce database load by caching the top posts for five minutes.
steps: Create an Azure Cache for Redis instance
Register Redis in Program.cs with the cache connection string
Cache the result of the top-posts query
Update a post and verify the cache eventually reflects the change
data.expectedOutcome: Repeated calls to the endpoint return cached results until expiration.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure Cache for Redis is a managed Redis service
Use `IDistributedCache` for ASP.NET Core caching abstractions
Cache hot, read-heavy, or expensive-to-compute data
Plan invalidation before caching mutable data
data.takeaway: Redis caching can dramatically reduce database load and response time with a small amount of C# code.
